body:
You are drafting dialogue for "Curse of Strahd", a single-player D&D 5e (2024 rules) computer game set in Barovia. I need you to write lines for ONE scene package at a time. Reply with plain text only: the lines under the node names given below, nothing else. Finish without sending messages to anyone else.

## The feature: Ezmerelda's Hunter's Ledger

Ezmerelda d'Avenir is a young Vistana monster hunter (long dark coat, rapier, a small crossbow with silver-headed bolts, a spyglass, and an oak-and-steel brace below her right knee where a werewolf took her leg). She was trained by Rudolph van Richten, the legendary hunter, who walked into the mists twelve years ago and has been calling himself Rictavio ever since (a loud half-elf showman at the Blue Water Inn in the town of Vallaki). She hunts the things that hunt people, and she is now an ally the player's party can talk to whenever they find her (at the shore of Lake Baratok by Van Richten's tower, on the switchback above the abbey, in the inn's stable yard in Vallaki, or beside them on the road once she has joined).

She keeps THE HUNTER'S LEDGER: a battered book of the valley's killers, each with a price on its head. She pays for proof, in the things a hunter has to give: silver-headed bolts, holy water, healing draughts, scrolls and potions made against the thing that was killed, and later a weapon from her wagon. The game records which of these killers the party has actually killed; the ledger pays for exactly those and nothing else. She names three names at a time: first any she can pay now, then hunts near where the party is, then the hardest hunt the party is ready for. There is no deadline and no penalty: the ledger is a reason to come back and talk to her, not a test. A hunt she briefs the party on is words only; nothing in her briefing forces a fight.

## Ezmerelda d'Avenir - voice bible

Quick, sardonic, practical; hunter's rules delivered as jokes. Teases, then means it. Calls Van Richten "Rudolph" and treats his legend with exasperated love. Pet phrases: "Say something a vampire wouldn't." "Silver first, questions never." "Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at." Funny through showman timing (she grew up in wagons that put on shows), self-mockery about her own missing parts, and her running complaint about her teacher's habits. Wants: the end of the vampire lord in the castle; to find Rudolph and have a word with him first. Fears: being too late again; being left behind again. Secret: she isn't sure she's as brave as her reputation, and has started to think that's wisdom. She never says the vampire lord's name aloud: she says "the count", "the castle", "the devil in the castle" or nothing. She never calls the party "kids" or "girl". She treats the party as capable colleagues.

Existing Ezmerelda lines (match this register; do not repeat them):
- "Stop there. Say something a vampire wouldn't say."
- "Ezmerelda d'Avenir. Vistani, when the wagons will have me. I hunt the things that hunt people. I'm very good at it, as you can tell from all the bits of me that are left."
- "Nobody with fangs has ever asked to buy silver. Not twice, anyway. Sit."
- "He's making tea. He's terrible at tea. Don't tell him; he thinks it's the only thing he's good at besides killing."
- "Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at. Rudolph says it'll kill me. Rudolph says a lot, from very far away."
- "I go first through doors. Not because I'm brave. Because I've got the leg that doesn't bleed."
- "Angels don't stitch. Whatever runs this abbey, it's been practising on people."
- "I go first through doors, I take the silver, and nobody calls me 'girl'."
- "Keep your heads down unless you want the dead upstairs to think you brought them a tournament."
- "Witches feed you before they hurt you, and anything posing in these fields is watching when you turn your back."
- "Keep to the crown of the road, and don't answer anything that calls your name from the trees."
- "The castle sends them down this road in ones and twos after dark, so listen for dragging feet before looking."

## The Narrator

An old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather. Second person, present tense. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn (irony, dread, dry joke). Never cruel. Concrete senses over adjectives (a smell, a sound, a temperature). No game terms: never "roll", "check", "DC", "HP", "level". No winks at the player.
Samples:
- "By a painted wagon, a woman in a long dark coat sits fixing silver heads to crossbow bolts. Below her right knee, a brace of oak and steel; her left hand is bandaged, and she smells faintly of burnt hair."
- "She doesn't look up. She lifts a small loaded crossbow off her knee instead and points it at you."

## Canon limits (important)

Use ONLY the facts given in this brief about every monster and place. Do not invent new monsters, names, places, victims, dates, past hunts of hers, or lore for any target. She is working from what the party tells her and what she has tracked, so she may be wrong-footed or dry about a target, but she may not state invented facts about it. No named characters beyond those in the brief. The party's own words are not in the lines: the party chooses menu options; Ezmerelda answers. Never mention flags, the game, a "ledger entry number", a level, dice, or the player.

## Format

One line per row, exactly: `Speaker [mood]: Text` where Speaker is Narrator or Ezmerelda. Moods allowed for Ezmerelda: smile, angry, sad, sly, weary (or no mood; most lines should have none; use a mood only where it clearly fits). The Narrator never has a mood. Each line is 1-2 sentences, ideally under 22 words in total, written to be spoken aloud by an actor: so NO stage directions in brackets or asterisks, NO "{name}" or other placeholders, no emoji, no markdown. Use plain ASCII punctuation (straight quotes, hyphens, no em dashes). Group the lines under the node names given below, each as a line `~ node_name`, in the order given. Where option texts (what the PARTY says) are requested, write them as `* text` rows under the node named, each under 12 words, in the party's voice ("we", or an imperative), no attitude beyond the intent given. Do not add nodes, code or commentary.

## This message: Ezmerelda's hub (the conversation around the ledger) - 29 lines and 6 option texts

The party can open this conversation wherever they find her: it is the same talk at the shore of Lake Baratok by the tower, on the switchback above the abbey, in the stable yard of the inn in Vallaki, or on the road (they click on her while she travels with them). So the lines must be neutral about where she is: no scenery, no "here". The first time, the party asks whether she has paying work, or clicks on her.

Her trust in the party is either low (the party has not done much for her yet) or warm (they have). The Narrator speaks only in the first node.

### Nodes

ledger_intro: Narrator x1 (she takes a battered, oilcloth-wrapped book out of her coat; the pages are crowded with names, some struck through), Ezmerelda x3 (what the book is: the valley's killers, each with a price; she only writes down what she has tracked herself; she pays for proof, not promises; a joke at her own expense or at Rudolph's. She names three at a time, because more is a to-do list and she has had enough of those). First meeting with this subject; no menu inside this node.
open_cold: Ezmerelda x1 (a business-like greeting when she still keeps the party at arm's length; wary, brisk; "What do you need?" in her own words)
open_warm: Ezmerelda x1 (a greeting when she trusts the party; dry warmth; she is glad to see them but would not say so)
ledger_ready: Ezmerelda x1 (she opens the book: at least one name is ready to be paid - she can smell fresh work on the party; invites them to pick)
ledger_hunt: Ezmerelda x1 (she opens the book: nothing is ready to pay, so these are the hunts she would take on in their place; the party picks one to hear about)
ledger_none: Ezmerelda x1 (she opens the book and has nothing to put in front of the party right now: either no hunt is in reach for them yet, or the near ones are done; come back when the valley has moved; not rude)
bye: Ezmerelda x1 (she closes the conversation; short, practical; an escape-the-valley hunter's rule as a joke)

rudolph_reunited: Ezmerelda x2 (the party asks how things are between her and Rudolph. They HAVE been reunited: the shouting and the hit on the arm have happened. Her answer: the new, awkward peace, still teasing, something true under it. Do not repeat these existing lines: "Quite well and completely unbearable. He's lecturing me on silver edges." / "He has a false moustache drying on his washstand and three books of terrible jokes by his bed.")
rudolph_waiting: Ezmerelda x2 (they have NOT met yet but she knows where he is: a showman at the inn in Vallaki. She is not ready to knock. Honest about being afraid without saying "afraid". Do not repeat: "He's inside the Blue Water Inn, and I'm out here hunting so I don't have to knock." / "Not until I've looked Rudolph in the eye.")
rudolph_seeking: Ezmerelda x2 (she does not know where he is, or the party has kept his secret from her. Twelve years of following; the ward he keyed to her alone; wry anger over worry. She is "good at looking")

leg_dead: Ezmerelda x2 (the party asks about her leg. The werewolf that took it, Kiril, is dead now - the party killed him. Be careful and specific: she says she does not feel what she thought she would. Facts you may use: it happened in the hills above Lake Zarovich when she was young and quick and stupid; the wolf was big, black and laughed with its mouth open; the brace of oak and steel is Rudolph's work and kicks harder than the old one; "Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at". Do not repeat: "That's the one who took my leg. Thank you. I wanted to do it myself. I find I don't mind that much, now.")
leg_alive: Ezmerelda x2 (same question, but Kiril is NOT dead: he is still up in the den, or the party has dealt with him some other way. Same facts. She tells it plainly and a little sideways, as someone who has told it too often; a hunter's lesson comes out of it)
vistani: Ezmerelda x3 (the party asks what she makes of the Vistani in this valley. She is Vistana but "when the wagons will have me": half inside, half out. Facts you may use: Madam Eva reads the cards at the camp by Tser Pool and has been "dealing her into other people's games" for years; there is another Vistani camp outside Vallaki; the Vistani guide, trade and tell fortunes for travellers in a valley that kills travellers. Do NOT explain why she left or how old she was (a later scene does that). Wry, a little wistful, one practical piece of advice for dealing with them)
view_a: Ezmerelda x2 (the party asks what she makes of where they are heading. The party is in the middle of the valley: villages, a reformed-looking abbey, a ruined manor of dead knights, a drowned village with a witch, hill roads with wolves. Her hunter's view: pick which of these to be careful about and why, and keep the lines hers: she repeats NO existing lines but may echo the spirit: do not draw steel on what you cannot finish; witches feed you first; angels do not stitch)
view_b: Ezmerelda x2 (same question, later: the party is going toward the high passes, the cold, and the temple beyond them. Facts you may use: the Tsolenka Pass is a cliff road with a bridge over a gorge where a roc hunts by day, and a guard tower whose ghostly watch has kept the gate shut for ages; beyond the pass is the Amber Temple, where the old powers sell gifts for a price. She distrusts gifts. Practical, warning, one joke)
view_c: Ezmerelda x2 (same question, last stage: the party is going to the castle. She will not make her plan until she sees the gates (a later scene does that); here she says so in her own way, plus one hard-won rule from Rudolph. Do not say the vampire lord's name)

### Option texts (what the party says), under these nodes

menu_ledger: `* ` ask whether she has paying work in her ledger (used each time after the first, so it also works as "let us see the ledger")
menu_rudolph: `* ` ask how things are with Rudolph
menu_leg: `* ` ask about her leg
menu_vistani: `* ` ask what she makes of the Vistani here
menu_view: `* ` ask what she makes of where we are heading
menu_bye: `* ` say goodbye

That is 29 lines and 6 option texts.

Narrator: She draws a battered book from her coat, unwrapping its oilcloth cover. The pages are crowded with names, and the best ones are struck through in black ink.
Ezmerelda: Every killer in this valley that I've tracked myself, and what I'll pay to see it dead.
Ezmerelda [sly]: I pay in silver, holy water, and remedies for proof, not promises - Rudolph taught me to count teeth before parting with coin.
Ezmerelda: I only give three names at a time, because four is a chore list and I left my teacher to escape those.

~ open_cold
Ezmerelda: Hands where I can see them and state your business. What do you need?

~ open_warm
Ezmerelda [smile]: Still breathing, all of you. Tell me what you need before my luck rubs off on you.

~ ledger_ready
Ezmerelda [sly]: You smell like smoke and fresh work. Point to the name you finished and let's settle the debt.

~ ledger_hunt
Ezmerelda: Nothing's owed yet, so here are the three hunts I'd take in your boots. Pick a name.

~ ledger_none
Ezmerelda [weary]: The near work is done and the rest will eat you alive today. Give the valley a day to move, then ask again.

~ bye
Ezmerelda: Silver first, questions never, and don't die between here and the next crossroads.

~ rudolph_reunited
Ezmerelda [weary]: My knuckles still ache from his arm, and he's already correcting how I oil my crossbow.
Ezmerelda [smile]: We're speaking, mostly in arguments, which is how Rudolph says he missed me too.

~ rudolph_waiting
Ezmerelda: Twelve years of chasing him through the mists, and all that's left is one painted wagon and an inn door.
Ezmerelda [weary]: It's easier to track a werewolf in the dark than to find out whether your teacher wanted to be found.

~ rudolph_seeking
Ezmerelda [angry]: Twelve years I've followed his tracks, right to a door he warded for my hands alone, and the old fox still isn't home.
Ezmerelda: Don't worry about him; I'm very good at looking, and when I find him he'll wish a monster had got there first.

~ leg_dead
Ezmerelda: I was young, quick, and stupid in the hills above Lake Zarovich when Kiril took it, laughing with his black jaws wide.
Ezmerelda [weary]: Rudolph built me this oak-and-steel brace that kicks twice as hard, and now that the wolf's dead, I mostly just feel lighter.

~ leg_alive
Ezmerelda: A big black wolf named Kiril took it in the hills above Lake Zarovich while I was busy being young, quick, and stupid.
Ezmerelda [sly]: Rudolph made me this oak-and-steel brace, and I learned the lesson: never swing at a mouth that's still laughing at you.

~ vistani
Ezmerelda: They're my blood when the wagons will have me, though trading and guiding travellers in a valley that eats them is a tight rope.
Ezmerelda [weary]: Between the camp outside Vallaki and Madam Eva dealing me into other people's card games at Tser Pool, I keep my distance.
Ezmerelda: Pay what they ask, don't steal from the horses, and never mistake a warm fire for a free favour.

~ view_a
Ezmerelda: Between the wolves on the hill roads, the drowned village's witch, and those dead knights in their ruined manor, pick your fights before drawing steel.
Ezmerelda: Keep sharpest around that abbey; whatever's playing at holiness up there has a butcher's hand with a needle.

~ view_b
Ezmerelda: Tsolenka Pass is a freezing cliff road where a roc hunts the gorge by day and a ghostly watch keeps the gate shut.
Ezmerelda [sly]: Past that is the Amber Temple, where old powers offer gifts for a price - and if you take free gifts here, I'm keeping my silver.

~ view_c
Ezmerelda: I don't make a plan for the castle until I'm looking at its gates; paper plans die on the drawbridge.
Ezmerelda: Just remember Rudolph's first rule for the count's house: know which window you're jumping out of before you open the door.

~ menu_ledger
* Let us see what work is in the ledger.

~ menu_rudolph
* How are things between you and Rudolph?

~ menu_leg
* Tell us what happened to your leg.

~ menu_vistani
* What do you make of the Vistani in this valley?

~ menu_view
* What do you make of where we are heading?

~ menu_bye
* We should get moving.

brief_<id>: Ezmerelda x2. The party asks her about a name that is STILL ALIVE. Use ONLY the target facts below.

Line 1: her reaction and a short hunter's story or aside about the name (a joke, a rule, a grudge, a regret - drawn only from the facts below and her voice; it must read right whether she was told or can smell it on them). ## This message: ledger names 1 to 7 - 28 lines and 14 option texts

### Name 1: `falls` - Dragan, the werewolf at Tser Falls
Facts: Tser Falls is where the River Ivlis throws itself off a cliff in a long white fall; a shelf of rock juts over the drop where the Barovians leave tokens for the drowned and the fallen. A werewolf named Dragan waits at the lip of the falls at night for travellers, with wolves (a dire wolf and some wolves). He is one of Kiril's pack (Kiril leads the werewolf pack that dens in the hills above Lake Zarovich; she has been hunting that pack for years, a few at a time). The party killed him there; long scratches in the rock show where he stood. Payment: silver-headed bolts, and something to stitch yourselves with (a healing draught).

### Name 2: `wagon` - the Tinker's Wagon
Facts: A green painted tinker's wagon stands at the crossroads on the Old Svalich Road, selling pots and trinkets (some of them taken from a haunted house). Travellers who bought from the tinker never came back down the road. The tinker, Iosif, used to be one of the Vistani; he sat on the board and never climbed down. The wagon is a mimic the size of a wagon; it kept Iosif alive at the front as bait for seven years; its sticky arms grab, its tailboard bites, it spits trinkets. The party killed it, and Iosif went back to the Vistani camp at Tser Pool. Payment: flasks of alchemist's fire, silver-headed bolts, and a healing draught.

### Name 3: `fowlers` - the count's fowlers on the hill trail
Facts: On the hill trail above Lake Zarovich, a silver cage hung in a dead pine with a raven in it that would not change back. It was a trap. The count's fowlers - vampire spawn, a leader and several more, with swarms of bats - waited in the branches for whoever came for the cage. The party killed them. (Ezmerelda knows only the trap and the fowlers, not whose cage or whose raven; she may have a hunter's opinion about cages.) Payment: holy water, silver-headed bolts, and a healing draught.

### Name 4: `vine` - the Vine Mother
Facts: The Seventh Row of a vineyard came up black every night and was picked bare by morning. It was a cutting of the old Gulthias tree, planted under the row by druids and grown into the row itself: a heaving mass of black vine-wood twice the height of a house. Its branches reach, its vines drag you in and squeeze, and it spits fermenting black wine. Smaller vine blights and needle blights grew around it. The party cut it down. Payment: a scroll that guards against plants, flasks of alchemist's fire, and a healing draught.

### Name 5: `morgantha` - Morgantha of Old Bonegrinder
Facts: Morgantha is a night hag who keeps Old Bonegrinder, a windmill on a crag between the village of Barovia and the town of Vallaki, with her two "daughters", who are hags too. She sold dream pastries from a cart at the village and kept in cages the children whose parents couldn't pay. She talks sugar and endearments, speaks of herself in the third person, fears being alone and fears sunlight on holy symbols. The party killed her and broke the coven. Payment: a scroll against fiends (hags are fiends), holy water, antitoxin, and a healing draught.

### Name 6: `wint` - Wintersplinter on Yester Hill
Facts: Wintersplinter is a tree blight on the crown of Yester Hill, the walking tree at the druids' stone circle; a green stone the size of a plum pulses in its split heartwood. The druids of the hill dug the mountain folk's dead out of the mounds at the foot of Yester Hill and stacked their skulls up the slope. The party destroyed Wintersplinter on the crown. Payment: flasks of alchemist's fire, bolts with a keener edge (magical bolts), and a healing draught.

### Name 7: `huntsman` - the Count's Huntsman
Facts: On cold nights a horn sounds in the Svalich woods, and in the morning whoever the count is displeased with lies under the crossroads gallows, run to death. The Huntsman is Toader, a poacher the count ran down himself in his first winter; he stood and turned at the crossroads and was made huntsman for it. Every quarry since has become one of his hounds; the Vistani have scratched the quarries' names on cairns by the road. He is a long grey undead man in a hunting coat gone black with weather, with a horn that frightens, a boar spear and black arrows; he rides with a nightmare mare and hounds that are dire wolves. The hunt ends under the gallows at moonrise. The party killed him and his hounds at the crossroads. Payment: a scroll that guards against the undead, a draught that blunts grave-cold (resistance to necrotic harm), and holy water.

Reply layout: first all the `brief_` and `claim_` nodes in the order given (brief_falls, claim_falls, brief_wagon, claim_wagon, ...), then the final block `~ options` with 14 `* ` option rows in the order ask_falls, claim_falls, ask_wagon, claim_wagon, and so on, each row prefixed with its id like `* ask_falls: text`.

That is 28 lines and 14 option texts.

Ezmerelda: Don't touch its pots or stand near the biting tailboard; burn it from range and send Iosif home to Tser Pool.

~ claim_wagon
Ezmerelda [weary]: Seven years stuck on that board while it ate travellers. Good that Iosif finally walked back to the Tser Pool camp.
Ezmerelda: That crosses the wagon off my ledger. Take the alchemist's fire and silver-headed bolts, and a healing draught for the road.

~ brief_fowlers
Ezmerelda: On the hill trail above Lake Zarovich, a raven in a silver cage hangs in a dead pine as bait.
Ezmerelda: The count's vampire spawn and bats wait in the branches above, so look up before touching cages and bring me word.

~ claim_fowlers
Ezmerelda: Anyone who hangs a silver cage in a dead pine deserves whatever climbs up the hill to answer it.
Ezmerelda [smile]: The count's fowlers are struck from the page. Take the holy water and silver-headed bolts; that healing draught is yours too.

~ brief_vine
Ezmerelda: The Seventh Row of the vineyard grew a Gulthias cutting twice house-height that drags you in and spits black wine.
Ezmerelda: Clear the needle and vine blights first, stay out of its reach, and tell me when that row stays down.

~ claim_vine
Ezmerelda: Druids plant one black stick and the whole row tries to drink you. I can smell that sour wine from here.
Ezmerelda: The Vine Mother is crossed out. Take the scroll against plants and the alchemist's fire; the healing draught is yours.

~ brief_morgantha
Ezmerelda: Morgantha and her two hag daughters keep Old Bonegrinder between Barovia village and Vallaki, caging children over unpaid dream pastries.
Ezmerelda [angry]: Never let all three sisters stand together, bring sunlight on holy symbols if you have it, and break that coven.

~ claim_morgantha
Ezmerelda: She always talked sugar while locking children in cages. A hag alone is a coward, and a dead coven stays quiet.
Ezmerelda: Morgantha's name is struck out for good. Take the scroll against fiends, the antitoxin, and the holy water; they're yours.

~ brief_wint
Ezmerelda: Up on Yester Hill's stone circle stands Wintersplinter, a walking tree blight with a pulsing green stone in its split heartwood.
Ezmerelda: Don't let the hill druids pen you against their stacked skulls; aim for the split wood and bring it down.

~ claim_wint
Ezmerelda: Digging the mountain folk from their mounds just to stack skulls for a walking tree. Even for this valley, that's ugly.
Ezmerelda: Wintersplinter is out of the ledger. Take these bolts with a keener edge and the alchemist's fire; they're yours.

~ brief_huntsman
Ezmerelda: Toader, the count's undead Huntsman, rides a nightmare with dire wolf hounds on cold nights until moonrise under the crossroads gallows.
Ezmerelda: Steady your nerve when his horn sounds, watch for his boar spear and black arrows, and end his hunt there.

~ claim_huntsman
Ezmerelda [sad]: Every quarry he ran down became another hound, and my people scratched their names on the road cairns for years.
Ezmerelda: Toader's hunt is struck from the book. Take the scroll against the undead and the draught against grave-cold; they're yours.
